questions.q: What kind of weather made the worst traveling for the horses?
choices: Streets slippery with frost or snow
Hot, sunny days with dusty roads
Light spring rain in the morning
Thick, foggy mornings by the river
questions.evidence: When the streets were slippery with frost or snow that was the worst of all for us horses

questions.q: Why did one mile on icy roads tire a horse more than four on a good road?
choices: They strained every muscle to keep from falling
The cabs were much heavier in the winter
The horses were given less food in the cold winter months
The icy roads were really much longer
questions.evidence: the fear of falling is more exhausting than anything else

questions.q: What did Jerry believe was best to keep a cabman warm?
choices: Dry clothes, good food, and a comfortable wife at home
Beer and spirits from the tavern on the corner
A thick coat and a hot fire in the shelter
Working fewer hours and staying home when cold
questions.evidence: dry clothes, good food, cheerfulness, and a comfortable wife at home

questions.q: What did little Dolly bring to her father on the stand?
choices: Hot soup or pudding that Polly had ready
A warm coat and scarf that Polly had knitted
A bag of oats for Jack and Captain
Letters from customers who wanted rides
questions.evidence: some hot soup or pudding Polly had ready

questions.q: What did the gentleman tell Jerry to do when he came up to hire the cab?
choices: Finish his soup and set the child safely down
Hurry, because he was late for an important train
Leave Dolly sitting in the cab while they drove
Drive him straight to the station at a gallop

questions.q: Why did Jerry call him "a real gentleman"?
choices: He had time and thought for a cabman and his child
He wore very fine clothes and a tall silk hat
He paid twice the fare and gave Dolly a coin
He owned many horses and treated them all well
questions.evidence: he has got time and thought for the comfort of a poor cabman and a little girl

questions.q: What did the carter do when his horses started to move off without him?
choices: He beat them brutally, even about the head
He gave them a treat to make them stand
He let them walk on and caught up with them later
He shouted for the police to catch them
questions.evidence: punished them brutally, even beating them about the head

questions.q: Mr. Wright talks about standing up for "the oppressed." Who are the oppressed?
choices: Those who are treated cruelly or unfairly
Those who are rich and very powerful
Those who are much too busy to help
Those who break the law and must be punished

questions.q: What is the gentleman's main belief about cruelty?
choices: If we can stop cruelty and do nothing, we share the guilt
People should mind only their own business
Only the police should ever deal with people who are cruel
Horses do not really feel pain like people do
questions.evidence: we make ourselves sharers in the guilt
